what_was_delivered: Migration 0091_an_unused_package_or_plan_may_be_deleted. Two SECURITY DEFINER blocker functions (iam_v2.internet_package_deletion_blockers, iam_v2.service_plan_deletion_blockers) count every reference to a package across ALL its revisions (grants, purchases, offer quotes, portal offers, vouchers, voucher batches, settlement mappings, the checkout-grace config and every published grace policy, guest accounts), and to a plan (every package revision built on any of its revisions, including superseded ones, and every grant). Two kernels (iam_v2.internet_package_delete_unused, iam_v2.service_plan_delete_unused) lock the row, re-count on the same function, refuse with the reasons, and otherwise remove the item and its revisions WITHOUT cascade; every foreign key stays ON DELETE NO ACTION as the backstop. Revision immutability admits a DELETE only from inside those kernels (a transaction-local flag AND current_user = the table owner). svc_edged holds EXECUTE on the four functions and DELETE on no catalogue table; the migration asserts that for every service role, and the grant is mirrored in deploy/gatep so a factory-clean install keeps it. edged answers deletability from the database and adds DELETE with password step-up, a bounded reason and an audit record; a use that appears while the dialog is open is a 409 carrying the reasons. Hotel Admin deletes when allowed and explains and offers Disable when not.

verification_live: Through the real runtime role, on PRE-LIVE: the p6-validation package (then still holding its scaffold grants) was REFUSED with its counts and HTTP 409; every operator plan in use was refused with its counts; a wrong step-up password was refused with HTTP 401 and deleted nothing. A throwaway plan and package were created: the plan was refused while the package version stood on it; the package was deletable and deleted (rows 0/0, then 404); the plan then became deletable and was deleted (rows 0/0). Both deletions were audited with their reason, and the catalogue, grant and purchase counts were identical before and after. A browser driving https://172.21.60.25 passed 12 of 12 package and plan checks, including the refusal dialog's real reasons and phone width.
scaffold_removal: SCOPE PROVEN BEFORE REMOVAL. An FK-closure walk over every foreign key (composite keys included) and a scan of every uuid, text and jsonb column found exactly 26 dependent rows, and each traced to the Phase-6 validation scope script: the stay P6-VALIDATION on the never-configured interface, two zero-amount ADMIN_GRANT purchases on it with no settlement mapping, their two terminated entitlements, two ended sessions with 0 bytes on a scaffold device, and their bindings, device authorisations, device rows, state transitions, device actions and one skipped interval. Every row was backed up as JSON to /root/scaffold-backup-20260924T225933Z on the appliance. REMOVAL: one transaction pinned to those exact ids, each DELETE asserting its exact row count, a guard that aborted if the set had changed, the family controlled-operation scopes opened as the guards require, and only the five append-only guard triggers disabled and re-enabled inside it; foreign-key enforcement stayed ON throughout. The first attempt rolled back entirely (pending deferred-trigger events blocked re-enabling a guard) and changed nothing; the second committed. A whole-schema row-count diff shows exactly the enumerated rows gone plus four controlled-operation scope tokens (the opener's own bookkeeping, removed by its hourly janitor) and nothing else. The never-configured PMS connection 6d5f0000-0000-4000-8000-000000000101 is gone. With nothing depending on it, the p6-validation package was then deleted THROUGH THE PRODUCT PATH (deletability yes, DELETE 200, audited), removing it and its one revision. NOT removed, because not authorised: the scaffold service plan p6-validation and the two scaffold devices.
protel_continuity: pmsd was not restarted and no PMS configuration was touched. Before and after the removal: CONNECTED, IN_SYNC, CONTINUOUS, room sign-in ready, 490 in house, nothing pending or awaiting review, pmsd active since 20:16:12Z, no warnings in its journal. The Protel interface ddff5d07 is now the only PMS interface on the appliance.
